claims.source: Using HSC specific markers, however, is confounded by the observations that in remission, patients in chronic phase restore Philadelphia chromosome-negative (Ph-) hematopoiesis (Bergamaschi et al., 1994; Carella et al., 1993; Claxton et al., 1992; Coulombel et al., 1983; Deininger, 2003), implying the co-existence of BCR::ABL1- HSCs and BCR::ABL1+ LSCs.
claims.evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: The proportion of BCR::ABL1- HSCs and BCR::ABL1+ LSCs varies across individuals and treatment stages.
claims.source: However, because their proportion varies across individuals and treatment stages (Mustjoki et al., 2013), and both LSCs and HSCs reside within similar immunophenotypic compartments (Lin-CD34+CD38-/low) (Eisterer et al., 2005; Petzer et al., 1996), discrimination between these populations – and thereby reliably estimating LSCs – remains difficult.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Both LSCs and HSCs reside within similar immunophenotypic compartments (Lin-CD34+CD38-/low).
claims.source: However, because their proportion varies across individuals and treatment stages (Mustjoki et al., 2013), and both LSCs and HSCs reside within similar immunophenotypic compartments (Lin-CD34+CD38-/low) (Eisterer et al., 2005; Petzer et al., 1996), discrimination between these populations – and thereby reliably estimating LSCs – remains difficult.
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: At diagnosis, Lin-CD34+CD38-/low BCR::ABL1+ cells could be divided into seven molecularly distinct subpopulations.
claims.source: This demonstrated that at diagnosis, Lin-CD34+CD38-/low BCR::ABL1+ cells could be divided into seven molecularly distinct subpopulations, each reflecting unique lineage and cell state signatures.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work (Warfvinge et al., 2017).

claims.claim: The proportions of BCR::ABL1+ LSC subpopulations changed dynamically upon therapy.
claims.source: Importantly, the proportions of BCR::ABL1+ LSC subpopulations changed dynamically upon therapy and only a few surface markers efficiently discriminated between BCR::ABL1+ vs. BCR::ABL1- cells.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work (Warfvinge et al., 2017).

claims.claim: CD26 was more frequently detected in the subpopulation most persistent during TKI treatment.
claims.source: Of these, despite being generally reduced in BCR::ABL1+ cells upon therapy, CD26 was more frequently detected in the subpopulation most persistent during TKI treatment.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work (Warfvinge et al., 2017).

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1+Lin-CD34+CD38-/lowCD45RA-cKIT-CD26+ cells are the most TKI-insensitive cells.
claims.source: The substantial treatment-induced changes observed within the stem cell population suggested that BCR::ABL1+ LSCs are themselves heterogeneous in terms of sensitivity to TKIs allowing us to define BCR::ABL1+Lin-CD34+CD38-/lowCD45RA-cKIT-CD26+ as the most TKI-insensitive cells.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work (Warfvinge et al., 2017).

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1+Lin-CD34+CD38-/lowCD45RA-cKIT-CD26+ cells are strikingly enriched after TKI therapy.
claims.source: Apart from being detected at diagnosis, these cells are strikingly enriched after TKI therapy (Warfvinge et al., 2017), a finding since confirmed in a transgenic mouse model (Shah et al., 2023), and in clinical observations documenting the long-term persistence of CD26+ cells in CML patients (Pacelli et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies including the authors' own work.

claims.claim: CD26+ cells persist long-term in CML patients.
claims.source: Apart from being detected at diagnosis, these cells are strikingly enriched after TKI therapy (Warfvinge et al., 2017), a finding since confirmed in a transgenic mouse model (Shah et al., 2023), and in clinical observations documenting the long-term persistence of CD26+ cells in CML patients (Pacelli et al., 2023).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pacelli et al., 2023.

claims.claim: CITE-seq was used to quantify global gene expression profiles and highly multiplexed cell-surface protein profiles simultaneously within the same cells from nine CML patients.
claims.source: Therefore, we used cellular indexing of transcriptomes and epitopes by sequencing (CITE-seq Stoeckius et al., 2017) to quantify the global gene expression program, and highly multiplexed cell-surface protein profile simultaneously within the same cells from nine CML patients.
claims.evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claims.claim: The CITE-seq analysis included >40 surface markers.
claims.source: The CITE-seq analysis combines single-cell RNA-seq with simultaneous staining for a panel of >40 antibodies conjugated to uniquely barcoded oligonucleotides (henceforth Antibody derived tags, ADTs) aimed to cover the spectrum of normal hematopoietic stem (CD34+CD38-/low fraction) and lineage progenitors (CD34+ enriched fraction, HSPCs) as well as surface markers reported to enrich for CML stem cells (Herrmann et al., 2014; Järås et al., 2010; Kinstrie et al., 2020; Landberg et al., 2018; Sadovnik et al., 2016; Warfvinge et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claims.claim: Scarf projection was used to map each individual CML cell to a Lin-CD34+ healthy bone marrow reference.
claims.source: To allow for accurate specification of LSPC heterogeneity without confounding effects generated from cell-type-irrelevant transcriptional signals related to BCR-ABL transformation per se, or inter-patient variability due to batch effects, we used Scarf projection (Dhapola et al., 2022) to map each individual CML cell to a Lin-CD34+ healthy bone marrow reference with a predefined heterogeneity.
claims.evidence: This describes the analytical approach used in the study.

claims.claim: The normal reference consisted of 4696 Lin-CD34+ cells from two age-matched healthy donors.
claims.source: To build a normal reference, we used our recently described CITE-seq profiles of Lin-CD34+ cells from normal BM from two age-matched healthy donors (henceforth, nBM) (Sommarin et al., 2021). The normal reference of 4696 Lin-CD34+ cells was visualized in a Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP, Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: This describes the reference dataset used in the study.

claims.claim: Eleven cell clusters were identified in the normal bone marrow reference consisting of primitive cells, lineage progenitors and cycling cells.
claims.source: We identified eleven cell clusters consisting of primitive cells, lineage progenitors and cycling cells in the UMAP, with near-to-equal distribution across the two nBM samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of the normal bone marrow reference, supported by Figure 1B and supplementary figure.

claims.claim: 14,274 Lin-CD34+ cells from nine CML patients were analyzed by CITE-seq.
claims.source: Following CITE-seq of 14,274 Lin-CD34+ cells from nine CML patients, the cells were projected onto the nBM reference and annotated by label-transfer.
claims.evidence: This describes the dataset analyzed in the study.

claims.claim: CML patients, in general, were enriched for basophil/mast cell, MEP, MkP clusters and depleted for primitive, MPP1, 2, and ly/pDC/Mono clusters compared to normal bone marrow.
claims.source: A comparison of abundance of clusters showed that CML patients, in general, were enriched for basophil/mast cell, MEP, MkP clusters and depleted for primitive, MPP1, 2, and ly/pDC/Mono clusters (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from comparing CML patients to normal bone marrow, supported by Figure 2B.

claims.claim: A set of 71 genes comprised a pan-CML signature shared among all cluster comparisons.
claims.source: In contrast, when considering genes differentially expressed in CML relative to nBM, and crucially shared among all the cluster comparisons, we identified a set of 71 genes that comprised a pan-cml signature.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from differential gene expression analysis.

claims.claim: 50 genes were found to be consistently up-regulated in CML stem and progenitors.
claims.source: Of the 71 genes, 50 genes were found to be consistently up-regulated in CML stem and progenitors.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from differential gene expression analysis, shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: 21 genes were specifically and consistently upregulated in all clusters across nBM versus CML.
claims.source: The analysis also identified 21 genes specifically and consistently upregulated in all clusters across nBM versus CML, and among others included DPY30 gene implicated in the maintenance of adult HSCs (Yang et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from differential gene expression analysis.

claims.claim: All clusters from the normal bone marrow reference samples were represented in each CML patient.
claims.source: By enumerating the proportion of molecularly defined clusters of individual patients, we found that all clusters from the normal bone marrow reference samples were represented in each patient.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the cluster analysis of individual patients.

claims.claim: There was remarkable heterogeneity between patients in terms of relative abundance of constituent clusters.
claims.source: However, there was remarkable heterogeneity between patients in terms of relative abundance of constituent clusters (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the cluster analysis of individual patients, supported by Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Treatment failure cases displayed a higher abundance of the molecularly defined primitive cluster compared to optimal responders at diagnosis.
claims.source: A focused comparison between optimal responders (CML 1–4) and treatment failure cases (CML 8–9) showed distinctive enrichment of specific cell clusters (Figure 3B), where failure cases displayed a higher abundance of the molecularly defined primitive cluster, multipotent progenitors 1 and 2, and myelo-lymphoid (My/Ly) and Ly/pDC/monocyte clusters at diagnosis.
claims.evidence: This is a key finding comparing treatment outcomes, supported by Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Treatment failure cases displayed a fourfold higher abundance of primitive cells compared to optimal responders at diagnosis.
claims.source: Among others, the most conspicuous changes between optimal responders and treatment failures were observed in the primitive cluster (fourfold higher in failures), and MEP and erythroid cluster (∼threefold higher in optimal).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative finding from comparing treatment outcomes.

claims.claim: Optimal responders had approximately threefold higher abundance of MEP and erythroid clusters compared to treatment failures at diagnosis.
claims.source: Among others, the most conspicuous changes between optimal responders and treatment failures were observed in the primitive cluster (fourfold higher in failures), and MEP and erythroid cluster (∼threefold higher in optimal).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative finding from comparing treatment outcomes.

claims.claim: Deconvolution of an independent bulk gene expression dataset from 59 CML patients showed a >threefold statistically significant enrichment of primitive cells in non-responders compared to responders.
claims.source: The deconvolution results demonstrated a heterogeneous cell composition across patients, and overall comparison of imatinib non-responders (n=18 out of 59) versus responders (n=41 out of 59) showed a >threefold statistically significant enrichment of primitive cells in non-responders (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from computational deconvolution of an independent dataset, supported by Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Primitive cells were rarely detected in peripheral blood in contrast to the bone marrow.
claims.source: Notably, the primitive cells were rarely detected in peripheral blood in contrast to the bone marrow, confirming the notion that cell type fractions differ in different tissues (Figure 3D), and the bone marrow is predictably a more reliable and abundant source of true primitive cells in CML.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the deconvolution analysis comparing bone marrow and peripheral blood.

claims.claim: CD25, CD26, and CD93 could only capture a fraction of the primitive cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, according to the ADT data, the established CML stem cell markers CD25, CD26, and CD93 could only capture a fraction of the primitive cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from analyzing ADT expression in primitive cells.

claims.claim: 6779 cells from the Lin-CD34+CD38-/low compartment from 8 CML patients were analyzed by CITE-seq.
claims.source: To further investigate the molecular and immunophenotypic heterogeneity within the primitive cluster we performed CITE-seq on the stem cell enriched Lin-CD34+CD38-/low compartment from the same patients (n=8; 6779 cells Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This describes the dataset analyzed for the stem cell enriched fraction.

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1- primitive cells were distinctly and consistently separated in the UMAP for each patient.
claims.source: Remarkably, subsequent matching of BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1- cell IDs to the primitive cells in the joint Lin-CD34+ and Lin-CD34+CD38-/low UMAPs (indicated by red and black cell color, respectively), indeed revealed that BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs were distinctly and consistently separated in the UMAP for each patient (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the multiomic analysis, supported by Figure 4B.

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1+ LSCs in all patients were positioned immediately juxtaposing the downstream progenitor populations forming a continuum of differentiation hierarchy.
claims.source: BCR::ABL1+ LSCs in all patients were positioned immediately juxtaposing the downstream progenitor populations forming a continuum of differentiation hierarchy characteristically observed in single-cell analysis of HSPCs (Pellin et al., 2019; Safi et al., 2022; Velten et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the UMAP analysis with citation support for the expected pattern.

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1- HSCs formed an isolated and distinct cluster clearly detached from the rest of the cells in the majority of patients.
claims.source: In contrast, BCR::ABL1- HSCs formed an isolated and distinct cluster clearly detached from the rest of the cells in the majority of patients, indicating that during the chronic phase of CML, active hematopoiesis is dominated by the BCR::ABL1+ LSCs while BCR::ABL1- HSCs reside in the bone marrow albeit in an inactive state with reduced contribution to hematopoiesis as previously suggested (Chen et al., 2023; Coulombel et al., 1983).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the UMAP analysis with interpretation supported by citations.

claims.claim: CD26, CD25, and CD93 displayed a 2–8 fold elevated expression in BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells compared to BCR::ABL1-.
claims.source: Moreover, using the ADT data we could validate the molecularly defined BCR::ABL1+ LSCs also by surface expression, with CD26, CD25, and CD93 displaying a 2–8 fold elevated expression in BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells as compared to BCR::ABL1-.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative finding from ADT analysis.

claims.claim: 244 genes were specifically upregulated in BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells.
claims.source: To gain an understanding of the nature of molecular program of BCR::ABL1+ vs. BCR::ABL1- primitive cells, we analyzed differentially expressed genes between the pooled primitive BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1- populations from all CML patients. This identified 244 genes specifically upregulated in BCR::ABL1+ and 180 genes upregulated in BCR::ABL1- cells (Figure 4C, Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from differential gene expression analysis, supported by Figure 4C.

claims.claim: 180 genes were upregulated in BCR::ABL1- primitive cells.
claims.source: To gain an understanding of the nature of molecular program of BCR::ABL1+ vs. BCR::ABL1- primitive cells, we analyzed differentially expressed genes between the pooled primitive BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1- populations from all CML patients. This identified 244 genes specifically upregulated in BCR::ABL1+ and 180 genes upregulated in BCR::ABL1- cells (Figure 4C, Supplementary file 6).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from differential gene expression analysis, supported by Figure 4C.

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells showed upregulated expression of IL2RA (CD25), DPP4 (CD26), IL1RAP, and LEPR (CD295).
claims.source: Interestingly, among genes up-regulated in BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells included the expression of established CML markers; IL2RA (CD25), DPP4 (CD26), and IL1RAP as well as LEPR (CD295) a receptor recently described as a novel marker for Lin-CD34+CD38-/low LSCs (Landberg et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from differential gene expression analysis with citation support for LEPR.

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1- cells displayed upregulated expression of CRHBP and CXCR4.
claims.source: In contrast, BCR::ABL1- cells displayed an up-regulated expression of the stem cell-related gene CRHBP (Barbieri et al., 2022; He et al., 2005) as well as CXCR4 important for homing and maintenance of normal HSCs (Sugiyama et al., 2006).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from differential gene expression analysis with citation support.

claims.claim: 28 unique markers were significantly up-regulated for either BCR::ABL1+ or BCR::ABL1- primitive cells.
claims.source: To specifically define the surface markers for their ability to capture BCR::ABL1+ vs. BCR::ABL1- primitive cells, we compared significantly up-regulated ADTs for either Lin-CD34+CD38-/low BCR::ABL1+ LSCs or BCR::ABL1- HSCs cells across patients and identified markers with consistent expression across the data set. We found 28 unique markers to be significantly up-regulated for either BCR::ABL1+ or BCR::ABL1- cells (black or red colored bars in Figure 4B, Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from ADT analysis, supported by Figure 5A.

claims.claim: 17 ADTs marked BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and were detected in at least one patient.
claims.source: Of these 28 markers, 17 ADTs marked BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and were detected in at least one patient.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from ADT analysis.

claims.claim: CD26 and CD25 were explicit and consistent markers of BCR::ABL1+ LSCs throughout the entire cohort.
claims.source: However, only CD26, and CD25 were explicit and consistent throughout the entire cohort.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from ADT analysis across all patients.

claims.claim: CD93 was present on BCR::ABL1+ LSCs in 7/8 patients.
claims.source: CD93 was present on BCR::ABL1+ LSCs in 7/8 patients and other previously suggested LSC markers like CD33 and CD56 specifically labeled BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells in only a fraction of the patients.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from ADT analysis across patients.

claims.claim: 11 ADTs were specifically detected in BCR::ABL1- primitive cells from at least one patient.
claims.source: In contrast, 11 ADTs were specifically detected in BCR::ABL1- primitive cells from at least one patient.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from ADT analysis.

claims.claim: CD35 with approximately fourfold elevated expression was the only marker found to be consistently specific for the BCR::ABL1- HSC population across all patients.
claims.source: Interestingly, CD35 with ~fourfold elevated expression as compared to BCR::ABL1+ LSCs was the only marker found to be consistently specific for the BCR::ABL1- HSC population across all patients.
claims.evidence: This is a key finding from ADT analysis across all patients.

claims.claim: CD35 captures all HSCs in healthy human hematopoiesis.
claims.source: Intriguingly, we recently showed that CD35 captures all HSCs in healthy human hematopoiesis and that stem cell activity as measured by xenotransplantation assays and epigenetic profiling is restricted to CD35+ HSCs (Sommarin et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work with citation.

claims.claim: Stem cell activity is restricted to CD35+ HSCs.
claims.source: Intriguingly, we recently showed that CD35 captures all HSCs in healthy human hematopoiesis and that stem cell activity as measured by xenotransplantation assays and epigenetic profiling is restricted to CD35+ HSCs (Sommarin et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work with citation.

claims.claim: CD26 showed the highest capture of the BCR::ABL1+ primitive cluster (>95%) with consistent capture percentage across patients.
claims.source: CD26 showed the highest capture of the BCR::ABL1+ primitive cluster (>95%) with a consistent capture percentage across patients (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative finding from ADT gating analysis, supported by Figure 5D.

claims.claim: CD25 captured >80% of the BCR::ABL1+ primitive cluster on average but displayed higher variability in capture efficiency compared to CD26 across patients.
claims.source: This was followed by CD25 which captured >80% of the BCR::ABL1+ primitive cluster on average but displayed higher variability in capture efficiency compared to CD26 across patients.
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative finding from ADT gating analysis.

claims.claim: The CD35+ gate showed a specific capture of approximately 50% of the BCR::ABL1- primitive cluster.
claims.source: In contrast, the CD35 + gate showed a remarkable specific capture of BCR::ABL1- primitive cluster (~50%) (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative finding from ADT gating analysis, supported by Figure 5D.

claims.claim: CD26+CD35- ADTs captured BCR::ABL1+ primitive LSC cluster at high purity.
claims.source: Predictably, whereas a combination of CD26+CD35- ADTs captured BCR::ABL1+ primitive LSC cluster at high purity, the CD26-CD35+ combination marked BCR::ABL1- primitive HSC cluster with no contamination of BCR::ABL1+ LSCs (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from ADT combination gating analysis, supported by Figure 5E.

claims.claim: CD26-CD35+ combination marked BCR::ABL1- primitive HSC cluster with no contamination of BCR::ABL1+ LSCs.
claims.source: Predictably, whereas a combination of CD26+CD35- ADTs captured BCR::ABL1+ primitive LSC cluster at high purity, the CD26-CD35+ combination marked BCR::ABL1- primitive HSC cluster with no contamination of BCR::ABL1+ LSCs (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from ADT combination gating analysis, supported by Figure 5E.

claims.claim: CD26+CD35- cells showed a strong signal for BCR::ABL1 expression by qPCR while CD26-CD35+ cells were BCR::ABL1low/negative.
claims.source: The analysis showed a strong signal within CD26+CD35- cells for BCR::ABL1 expression while CD26-CD35+ cells were BCR::ABL1low/negative, validating the capacity of the combination of CD26 and CD35 to separate BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1- stem cells at diagnosis as well as after second generation TKI therapy.
claims.evidence: This is a validation finding using qPCR, shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Lin-CD34+CD38-/lowCD26+CD35- cells from CML patients at diagnosis displayed a strong signal for GAS2 by qPCR.
claims.source: In addition, real-time qPCR analysis confirmed that Lin-CD34+CD38-/lowCD26+CD35- cells from CML patients at diagnosis displayed a strong signal for GAS2 (Figure 6B), one of the top genes from the CITE-seq BCR::ABL1+ LSC signature (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is a validation finding using qPCR, shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: CD26+CD35- cells maintained GAS2 expression following 3 months of Bosutinib therapy.
claims.source: Furthermore, CD26+CD35- cells maintained GAS2 expression following 3 months of Bosutinib therapy (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from qPCR analysis after treatment, shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: GAS2 has been linked to CML disease progression, cell cycle control, apoptosis, and response to Imatinib.
claims.source: GAS2 has previously been linked to CML disease progression, cell cycle control, apoptosis, and response to Imatinib (Janssen et al., 2005; Radich et al., 2006; Zhou et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: LSC and HSC populations were indistinguishably deeply quiescent with average times to first division of 80–100 hr in culture.
claims.source: However, LSC and HSC populations were indistinguishably deeply quiescent with average times to first division of 80–100 hr in culture (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D–C).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from in vitro division kinetics experiments.

claims.claim: There was no distinct difference in cell cycle status between BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs.
claims.source: Moreover, cell cycle analysis was performed by gating the corresponding cell populations in the Lin-CD34+CD38-/low CITE-seq data using ADTs. In accordance with the in vitro study, there was no distinct difference in cell cycle status between the populations (Figure 5—figure supplement 2E–F).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from cell cycle analysis of CITE-seq data.

claims.claim: There was a substantially higher ratio of CD26+CD35- LSCs over CD26-CD35+ HSCs at diagnosis in prospective treatment failures compared to optimal responders.
claims.source: Intriguingly, we noted a substantially higher ratio of CD26+CD35- LSCs over CD26-CD35+ HSCs at diagnosis in prospective treatment failures compared to the bone marrow of optimal responders, both using CITE-seq ADTs as well as in FACS analysis for CD26 and CD35 (Figure 6C–D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This is a key finding comparing treatment outcomes, supported by Figure 6C-D.

claims.claim: Following three months of TKI therapy, the percentage of BCR::ABL1+ CD26+CD35- cells decreased in both optimal responders and treatment failures.

claims.evidence: This is a finding from FACS analysis after treatment.

claims.claim: The stem cell compartment of optimal responders was dominated by healthy HSCs at three months following treatment.
claims.source: The stem cell compartment of optimal responders was dominated by healthy HSCs at three months following treatment.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from FACS analysis after treatment.

claims.claim: The stem cell population of failure patients still comprised of CD26+CD35- LSCs without re-establishment of HSCs at three months following treatment.
claims.source: In contrast, the stem cell population of failure patients still comprised of CD26+CD35- LSCs without re-establishment of HSCs and restoration of normal hematopoiesis (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This is a finding from FACS analysis after treatment, shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: CML patients at diagnosis contain both BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSC within the Lin-CD34+CD38-/low immunophenotypic compartment.
claims.source: Moreover, longstanding observations have revealed that CML patients at diagnosis contain both BCR::ABL1+ LSCs vs. BCR::ABL1- HSC within the Lin-CD34+CD38-/low immunophenotypic compartment, and BCR::ABL1+ LSCs suppress residual normal HSCs (Chen et al., 2023; Coulombel et al., 1983).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: BCR::ABL1+ LSCs suppress residual normal HSCs.
claims.source: Moreover, longstanding observations have revealed that CML patients at diagnosis contain both BCR::ABL1+ LSCs vs. BCR::ABL1- HSC within the Lin-CD34+CD38-/low immunophenotypic compartment, and BCR::ABL1+ LSCs suppress residual normal HSCs (Chen et al., 2023; Coulombel et al., 1983).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: A lower fraction of BCR::ABL1- normal stem cells at diagnosis and during therapy relates to hematological toxicity with delayed or compromised restoration of Ph-negative hematopoiesis upon successful response to TKIs.
claims.source: Predictably, a lower fraction of BCR::ABL1- normal stem cells at diagnosis and during therapy relates to hematological toxicity with delayed or compromised restoration of Phneg hematopoiesis upon successful response to TKIs (Janssen et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: Prospective optimal responders to TKI treatment had a higher content of BCR::ABL1-CD26-CD35+ cells at diagnosis compared to treatment failures.
claims.source: Prospective optimal responders to TKI treatment had a higher content of BCR::ABL1-CD26-CD35+ cells at diagnosis, and 3 months following therapy versus the treatment failures.
claims.evidence: This is a finding from the study comparing treatment outcomes.

claims.claim: Not all LSC subpopulations are equally sensitive to BCR::ABL1 inhibition.
claims.source: Intriguingly, one of the emerging principles from the single-cell studies has been that not all LSC subpopulations are equally sensitive to BCR::ABL1 inhibition; while a majority of the LSCs are depleted, at least a fraction survives (Giustacchini et al., 2017; Warfvinge et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies including the authors' own work.

claims.claim: There is an overall reduction in BCR::ABL1+ Lin-CD34+CD38-/low cells upon commencing TKI therapy.
claims.source: This is corroborated by an overall reduction in BCR::ABL1+ Lin-CD34+CD38-/low cells but a striking enrichment of cKIT-CD26+ subpopulation displaying primitive and quiescent molecular program upon commencing TKI therapy (Warfvinge et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claims.claim: There is a striking enrichment of cKIT-CD26+ subpopulation displaying primitive and quiescent molecular program upon commencing TKI therapy.
claims.source: This is corroborated by an overall reduction in BCR::ABL1+ Lin-CD34+CD38-/low cells but a striking enrichment of cKIT-CD26+ subpopulation displaying primitive and quiescent molecular program upon commencing TKI therapy (Warfvinge et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claims.claim: Patients with activated immune signature at diagnosis are more likely to optimally respond to TKIs.
claims.source: The observations that patients with activated immune signature at diagnosis are more likely to optimally respond to TKIs (Radich et al., 2023) serve as apt reminder for collective analyses.
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claims.claim: The pan-CML signature included CD81, a surface marker previously implicated in CML.
claims.source: This included a constellation of genes such as surface markers, CD81 (Quagliano et al., 2020), nucleoside diphosphate kinase with transcriptional regulatory activity, NME2 (Kar et al., 2012; Thakur et al., 2009; Thakur et al., 2014; Thakur et al., 2011; Tschiedel et al., 2012; Tschiedel et al., 2008; Yadav et al., 2014) previously implicated in CML, genes of histone family, and components of SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex, BRD7 (Kaeser et al., 2008), as well as genes of histone methyltransferase family, KMT3A and 5 A (Husmann and Gozani, 2019).

results.result: The authors used CITE-seq to analyze 14,274 Lin-CD34+ cells from nine CML patients with >40 surface markers, mapping cells to a normal bone marrow reference of 4,696 cells from two healthy donors that contained 11 distinct cell clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C27-C32 describe the core methodology and reference dataset. The approach is well-documented with appropriate sample sizes, clear description of the analytical pipeline using Scarf projection, and validation through figures. The methodology is sound and reproducible.

results.result: Each CML patient harbored a unique composition of stem and progenitor cells at diagnosis, with all reference clusters represented but remarkable heterogeneity in relative abundance across patients.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C37-C38 are supported by the CITE-seq analysis and label transfer approach shown in Figures 2A and 3A. The finding of inter-patient heterogeneity is clearly demonstrated through individual UMAPs and quantification of cluster proportions.

results.result: Treatment failure patients had a fourfold higher abundance of molecularly defined primitive cells at diagnosis compared to optimal responders, while optimal responders had approximately threefold higher MEP and erythroid clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C39-C41 present quantitative comparisons between treatment groups supported by Figure 3B. The fourfold and threefold differences are explicitly stated and visually demonstrated. However, statistical testing details and sample sizes (n=4 optimal, n=2 failures) are limited, which could affect generalizability.

results.result: Deconvolution of an independent bulk gene expression dataset from 59 CML patients showed >threefold statistically significant enrichment of primitive cells in non-responders, with primitive cells rarely detected in peripheral blood compared to bone marrow.
results.evaluation: Claims C42-C43 are supported by computational deconvolution using CIBERSORTx on an independent dataset (GSE14671), providing external validation. The tissue-specific distribution finding strengthens the biological interpretation. Statistical significance is stated though detailed p-values are not provided in the text.

results.result: CML patients were enriched for basophil/mast cell, MEP, and MkP clusters and depleted for primitive and MPP clusters compared to normal bone marrow. A pan-CML signature of 71 genes (50 up-regulated, 21 down-regulated) was identified across all clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C36 describe differential cluster abundance and gene expression patterns supported by Figures 2B and 2D. The pan-CML signature approach of identifying genes consistently changed across all clusters is methodologically sound and avoids bias from numerically dominant clusters.

results.result: Analysis of 6,779 Lin-CD34+CD38-/low cells from 8 CML patients revealed that BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs were distinctly separated in UMAP space, with LSCs forming a continuum with progenitors while HSCs formed isolated clusters.
results.evaluation: Claims C45-C48 describe the stem cell-enriched fraction analysis supported by Figure 4B and supplementary figures. The distinct spatial separation and biological interpretation are well-supported by the multiomic data and consistent with cited literature on hematopoietic hierarchy.

results.result: Differential gene expression analysis identified 244 genes upregulated in BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells (including IL2RA/CD25, DPP4/CD26, IL1RAP, LEPR) and 180 genes upregulated in BCR::ABL1- cells (including CRHBP and CXCR4).
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C53 are supported by Figure 4C and differential expression analysis. The identification of known CML markers in the BCR::ABL1+ signature provides validation, while the BCR::ABL1- signature includes known HSC-related genes, supporting biological validity.

results.result: Among 28 surface markers differentially expressed between BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1- primitive cells, CD26 and CD25 were consistent markers of LSCs across all patients, while CD35 with ~fourfold elevated expression was the only consistent marker of HSCs across all patients.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C59 describe systematic ADT analysis supported by Figures 4B and 5A. The identification of CD35 as a consistent HSC marker is particularly novel and well-supported. The quantification of marker consistency across patients strengthens the findings.

results.result: BCR::ABL1+ LSCs can be distinctly separated as CD26+CD35- (capturing >95% of BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells) and BCR::ABL1- HSCs as CD26-CD35+ (capturing ~50% of BCR::ABL1- primitive cells) with no contamination between populations.
results.evaluation: Claims C7-C8, C62-C66 present the key methodological advance supported by Figure 5D-E. The high capture efficiency and purity are well-documented through ADT gating analysis. This represents a novel and practical approach for separating these populations.

results.result: qPCR validation confirmed that CD26+CD35- cells showed strong BCR::ABL1 expression while CD26-CD35+ cells were BCR::ABL1low/negative, and CD26+CD35- cells maintained GAS2 expression at diagnosis and after 3 months of Bosutinib therapy.
results.evaluation: Claims C67-C69 provide orthogonal validation of the CITE-seq findings using qPCR, supported by Figure 6A-B. The validation at both diagnosis and post-treatment strengthens confidence in the marker combination. GAS2 expression provides additional molecular validation.

results.result: The LSC/HSC ratio was substantially higher in treatment failures compared to optimal responders at diagnosis and after 3 months of TKI therapy. After treatment, optimal responders were dominated by healthy HSCs while failure patients retained CD26+CD35- LSCs without HSC re-establishment.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C10, C73-C76, C80 link the CD26/CD35 markers to treatment outcomes, supported by Figure 6C-E. The longitudinal analysis strengthens the clinical relevance. However, sample sizes are limited (n=6 optimal, n=5 failures) and statistical details could be more comprehensive.

results.result: LSC and HSC populations were indistinguishably deeply quiescent with average times to first division of 80-100 hours in culture, with no distinct difference in cell cycle status between BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C72 are supported by in vitro division kinetics experiments and cell cycle analysis of CITE-seq data shown in supplementary figures. The finding that both populations are similarly quiescent is important for understanding TKI resistance mechanisms.

results.result: CD26, CD25, and CD93 displayed 2-8 fold elevated expression in BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells compared to BCR::ABL1- cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C49 provides quantitative validation of known CML markers in the BCR::ABL1+ population using ADT data. The fold-change range is clearly stated and supports the use of these markers for LSC identification.

results.result: Established CML stem cell markers CD25, CD26, and CD93 could only capture a fraction of the primitive cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C44 is supported by Figure 3—figure supplement 2C showing incomplete capture of primitive cells by these markers. This finding motivates the need for the CD26/CD35 combination approach and highlights limitations of existing markers.

results.result: The primitive fraction in CML patients is a mixture of molecularly distinct BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs in variable ratio across patients.
results.evaluation: Claim C6 summarizes a key finding supported by the multiomic analysis shown in Figures 4 and 5. The variable ratio across patients is demonstrated through individual patient UMAPs and quantification, highlighting inter-patient heterogeneity.

results.result: CD62L and CD10 were present on BCR::ABL1- HSCs in 6/8 and 5/8 patients respectively. CD35 expression divided CD26- BCR::ABL1- primitive cells into CD35+ and CD35- fractions, with CD26-CD35- likely representing non-leukemic MPPs.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C94, C96-C97 describe additional surface marker patterns and hierarchical relationships. The interpretation of CD26-CD35- cells as MPPs (C96) is reasonable based on the HSC hierarchy literature cited, though this remains somewhat inferential.

results.result: Background claims about CML biology, LSC persistence, treatment challenges, and limitations of current monitoring methods.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C11-C20 present established knowledge about CML supported by appropriate citations. These provide context for the study but are not novel findings. The citations appear appropriate for the claims made.

results.result: Prior work from the authors and others on CML LSC heterogeneity, CD26+ cells, CD35+ HSCs, and various molecular markers and mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C21-C26, C60-C61, C70, C77-C95 cite prior work that provides foundation for the current study. The citations appear appropriate and accurate. These claims establish the rationale and build on previous findings but are not novel results from this manuscript.

results.result: Each CML patient harbored a unique composition of stem and progenitor cells at diagnosis, with all normal bone marrow reference clusters represented in each patient but with remarkable heterogeneity in relative abundance between patients.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding, with one reviewer stating 'substantial cellular heterogeneity was observed at diagnosis, suggesting that this is a hallmark of CML' and another noting the study demonstrates 'heterogeneity of stem and progenitor cell composition at diagnosis.' The editor's summary also highlights this as a fundamental insight.

results.result: Treatment failure cases displayed markedly higher abundance of molecularly defined primitive cells at diagnosis compared to optimal responders (fourfold higher), while optimal responders had approximately threefold higher abundance of MEP and erythroid clusters. This was validated in an independent bulk gene expression dataset showing >threefold enrichment of primitive cells in non-responders.
results.evaluation: All reviewers explicitly support this finding. One reviewer states 'patients with treatment failure after 12 months of therapy demonstrate increased frequency of molecularly defined primitive cells at diagnosis' and notes 'These results were validated by deconvolution of an independent previously published dataset.' Another reviewer emphasizes the data 'demonstrating convincingly that optimal responders and patients with treatment failure display significant differences in the proportion of primitive cells at diagnosis.'

results.result: The primitive fraction in CML patients is a mixture of molecularly distinct BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs in variable ratio across patients. BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs were distinctly and consistently separated in UMAP analysis, with BCR::ABL1+ LSCs positioned juxtaposing downstream progenitors while BCR::ABL1- HSCs formed isolated clusters detached from other cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding as a major contribution. One reviewer states 'The major new contribution of this study is the use of gene expression profiles to distinguish BCR-ABL+ and BCR-ABL- populations within CML primitive stem cell clusters' and notes the approach 'allowed them to show an association between the ratio of BCR-ABL+ vs BCR-ABL- primitive cells and TKI response.'

results.result: CD26 and CD25 were explicit and consistent markers of BCR::ABL1+ LSCs throughout the entire cohort, with CD26 showing >95% capture and CD25 capturing >80% on average. CD35 with approximately fourfold elevated expression was the only marker consistently specific for BCR::ABL1- HSCs across all patients, capturing approximately 50% of the BCR::ABL1- primitive cluster.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this finding as a key contribution. One reviewer states 'The finding that BCR/ABL+ versus negative LSCs display distinct surface markers is also key and will allow for more detailed interrogation of these cell populations at a molecular level.' Another notes the authors 'determined that a combination of CD26 and CD35 cell surface markers could be used to prospectively isolate the two populations.'

results.result: CD26+CD35- ADTs captured BCR::ABL1+ primitive LSCs at high purity while CD26-CD35+ combination marked BCR::ABL1- primitive HSCs with no contamination of BCR::ABL1+ LSCs. This was validated by qPCR showing strong BCR::ABL1 signal in CD26+CD35- cells while CD26-CD35+ cells were BCR::ABL1low/negative.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this validation, with one stating 'the authors have shown that CD26 and CD35 expression can consistently identify BCR-ABL+ versus BCR-ABL- cells.' The qPCR validation is noted as confirming the capacity of the marker combination to separate the populations.

results.result: The ratio of LSC/HSC was substantially higher in prospective treatment failures compared to optimal responders at diagnosis and following 3 months of TKI therapy. Following treatment, optimal responders' stem cell compartment was dominated by healthy HSCs while failure patients still comprised CD26+CD35- LSCs without re-establishment of HSCs.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this finding. One reviewer notes the study showed 'The relative proportion of CD26-CD35+ (BCR:ABL-) primitive stem cells was higher in optimal responders compared to treatment failures, both at diagnosis and following 3 months of TKI therapy.' Another emphasizes the data demonstrate 'the ratio of BCR-ABL+ versus negative LSCs' differs between responders and failures.

results.result: CITE-seq was used to quantify global gene expression profiles and >40 surface markers simultaneously from 14,274 Lin-CD34+ cells from nine CML patients, with cells projected onto a normal bone marrow reference of 4,696 Lin-CD34+ cells from two healthy donors containing eleven identified cell clusters.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the methodology, with one stating 'The studies are carefully conducted and the results are very clearly presented' and noting 'the application of single-cell multi-omics using CITE-Seq' as a strength. However, one reviewer notes 'The number of samples studied by CITE-Seq is limited' and another states 'CITE-seq was performed in only 9 CML patient samples and 2 healthy donors. Additional samples would greatly strengthen the very interesting and notable findings.'

results.result: CML patients were enriched for basophil/mast cell, MEP, MkP clusters and depleted for primitive, MPP1, 2, and ly/pDC/Mono clusters compared to normal bone marrow. A pan-CML signature of 71 genes was identified, with 50 genes consistently up-regulated in CML stem and progenitors and 21 genes upregulated in normal bone marrow.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not explicitly critique these findings and the editor's summary notes the study's 'robust methodology' provides 'compelling evidence for the identified associations between cellular composition and treatment outcome,' implicitly accepting these characterization results.

results.result: 244 genes were specifically upregulated in BCR::ABL1+ primitive cells (including established CML markers CD25, CD26, IL1RAP, and LEPR) while 180 genes were upregulated in BCR::ABL1- primitive cells (including stem cell-related genes CRHBP and CXCR4).
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these differential expression findings. The methodology is described as 'carefully conducted' and the results as 'very clearly presented,' suggesting acceptance of the gene expression analysis.

results.result: Lin-CD34+CD38-/lowCD26+CD35- cells from CML patients displayed strong signal for GAS2 by qPCR at diagnosis and maintained GAS2 expression following 3 months of Bosutinib therapy. GAS2 has been linked to CML disease progression, cell cycle control, apoptosis, and response to Imatinib.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge this validation finding. The qPCR validation is part of the overall validation approach that reviewers affirm, with one noting 'the authors have confirmed their key observations in additional samples.'

results.result: LSC and HSC populations were indistinguishably deeply quiescent with average times to first division of 80–100 hr in culture, and there was no distinct difference in cell cycle status between BCR::ABL1+ LSCs and BCR::ABL1- HSCs.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these findings about cell cycle status. The overall methodology is affirmed as 'carefully conducted,' suggesting acceptance of these supporting observations.

results.result: Primitive cells were rarely detected in peripheral blood in contrast to bone marrow, and established CML stem cell markers CD25, CD26, and CD93 could only capture a fraction of the primitive cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these observations. These findings support the rationale for the study's approach and are implicitly accepted as part of the overall methodology that reviewers describe as robust.

comparisons.comparison: Both evaluate the core CITE-seq methodology (C27-C32). OpenEval finds the approach well-documented and reproducible. Peer reviewers affirm the methodology as 'carefully conducted' with 'very clearly presented' results, but note the limited sample size (9 CML patients, 2 healthy donors) as a weakness requiring additional samples to strengthen findings.

Both evaluate inter-patient heterogeneity findings (C4, C37-C38). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers fully support this finding, with peer reviewers explicitly stating 'substantial cellular heterogeneity was observed at diagnosis, suggesting that this is a hallmark of CML' and highlighting it as a fundamental insight.

Both evaluate treatment outcome associations with primitive cell frequencies (C5, C39-C41). OpenEval notes support but raises concerns about limited statistical details and small sample sizes (n=4 optimal, n=2 failures). Peer reviewers strongly support the finding (C42 also included in peer evaluation), emphasizing validation through independent dataset deconvolution and describing the evidence as 'convincing.'

Both address deconvolution validation (C42-C43). OpenEval supports the external validation approach though notes limited p-value details. Peer reviewers support these observations (C43, C44) as part of the study rationale, implicitly accepting them within the robust methodology.

Both evaluate differential cluster abundance and gene expression patterns (C33-C36). OpenEval finds the pan-CML signature approach methodologically sound. Peer reviewers do not explicitly critique these findings and implicitly accept them as part of the 'robust methodology' providing 'compelling evidence.'

Both evaluate BCR::ABL1+ and BCR::ABL1- population separation (C46-C48 overlap, plus C6-C8 in peer review). OpenEval supports the stem cell-enriched fraction analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as a 'major new contribution,' emphasizing the use of gene expression profiles to distinguish populations and show association with TKI response.

Both evaluate differential expression signatures (C50-C53). OpenEval supports the identification of known CML markers in BCR::ABL1+ signature and HSC-related genes in BCR::ABL1- signature. Peer reviewers do not challenge these findings and describe the methodology as 'carefully conducted' with 'very clearly presented' results.

Both evaluate ADT analysis and CD26/CD35 marker identification (C56-C57, C59 overlap). OpenEval highlights CD35 as a novel HSC marker with strong quantitative support. Peer reviewers explicitly support this as a 'key contribution,' noting it 'will allow for more detailed interrogation of these cell populations at a molecular level.'

Both evaluate the CD26/CD35 sorting approach (C62-C64 overlap, plus C7-C8 in OpenEval). OpenEval emphasizes high capture efficiency and purity as a novel practical advance. Peer reviewers affirm this finding overlaps with their R4 evaluation, noting the marker combination can 'prospectively isolate the two populations.'

OpenEval R9 also addresses validation aspects (C65-C66 overlap with peer R5). OpenEval supports the ADT gating analysis documentation. Peer reviewers affirm 'CD26 and CD35 expression can consistently identify BCR-ABL+ versus BCR-ABL- cells' with qPCR validation confirming the marker combination's capacity.

Both evaluate qPCR validation (C67-C69, with C67 overlap). OpenEval emphasizes orthogonal validation at diagnosis and post-treatment with GAS2 expression providing additional molecular validation. Peer reviewers affirm this as part of confirming 'key observations in additional samples.'

Both evaluate qPCR validation findings (C68-C69 overlap). OpenEval supports the validation strengthening confidence in the marker combination. Peer reviewers affirm the validation without challenge, noting it confirms the capacity to separate populations.

Both evaluate longitudinal treatment outcome associations (C9-C10, C73-C76, C80). OpenEval supports the clinical relevance but notes limited sample sizes (n=6 optimal, n=5 failures) and calls for more comprehensive statistical details. Peer reviewers explicitly support the finding, emphasizing differences in CD26-CD35+ primitive stem cell proportions between responders and failures at both diagnosis and 3 months post-treatment.

Both evaluate cell cycle/quiescence findings (C71-C72). OpenEval supports these findings as important for understanding TKI resistance mechanisms. Peer reviewers do not challenge these observations and implicitly accept them as part of the 'carefully conducted' methodology.

OpenEval evaluates quantitative validation of known CML markers (C49) with clear fold-change ranges supporting LSC identification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

Both address limitations of existing markers (C44). OpenEval supports this finding as motivating the CD26/CD35 approach. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this observation (C44 in their R12) as part of the study rationale within the robust methodology.

Both address variable BCR::ABL1+/- ratios across patients (C6). OpenEval supports this finding demonstrating inter-patient heterogeneity. Peer reviewers include C6 in their evaluation of the major contribution regarding population separation and its association with TKI response.

OpenEval evaluates additional surface marker patterns and hierarchical relationships (C91-C94, C96-C97), noting the CD26-CD35- interpretation as MPPs is reasonable but somewhat inferential. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
